title: LinkedIn Pipeline Readiness Score
subtitle: Measure how well your ICP clarity, content, outreach, and pipeline system work together to turn LinkedIn into a real source of revenue.

answers.label: I know their job title and general industry
I know their goals and a few common pain points
I know what they've tried before and why it hasn't worked
I know their frustrations, what finally makes them take action, and the objections that stop them from buying
I know all of that AND what each individual buyer persona within an account actually cares about

low.headline: Your message can't land if you don't know exactly who you're talking to
low.text: Before you publish one more post or send one more outreach message, get clear on your ICP — not just their title and industry, but what they've tried, what frustrated them, and what finally makes them take action. Right now your messaging is probably blending into the noise. This is the most fixable thing in your business, and it changes everything downstream.
steps: Interview 3–5 past or current clients and ask them three things: what were you struggling with before we worked together, what had you already tried, and what finally made you decide to do something about it
Write a one-paragraph ICP description that goes beyond title and industry — include what they want, what they've tried, what frustrates them, and what finally makes them move
Rewrite your LinkedIn headline using the exact words your clients used in those conversations, not your own

mid.headline: You know your client — now sharpen how you talk to them
mid.text: You have a real foundation here. You know who you're after. The gap is getting your messaging tight enough that your ideal client reads your content and immediately feels like you wrote it specifically for them. That's the difference between content that gets likes and content that generates inbound leads.
steps: Pull your last 10 posts and honestly ask: does each one speak to a specific frustration my ICP has, or is it general industry content that anyone could have written?
Ask a current client to read your LinkedIn about section and tell you what stands out — and what's missing from their perspective
Pick the one buyer persona most likely to close and build three posts this month built entirely around their biggest frustration

high.headline: Your ICP clarity is a real competitive edge — keep building on it
high.text: Most people post and hope the right client finds them. You actually know who you're talking to and what they need to hear. That's rare, and it shows in your results. Now make sure that clarity is consistently embedded across everything you publish — not just when you're actively thinking about it.
steps: Document your ICP profile so it stays consistent as you create more content or bring in support — clarity that only lives in your head is a bottleneck
Map your ICP insights to every layer of your content: your hooks, your body copy, and your calls to action should all be pulling in the same direction
Look at your inbound leads from the last 90 days — are the right people showing up? If not, one detail in your ICP description is off and worth revisiting

low.headline: Your content is working hard but not working smart
low.text: If people aren't responding to your content with leads and real conversations, it's not a volume problem. More posts with the same approach won't fix it. Content that actually builds a pipeline has to earn attention AND give buyers a clear reason to take the next step. Right now, one of those pieces is missing — and adding more content without fixing it just amplifies the gap.
steps: Audit your last 10 posts: how many were designed to drive a specific action — visit my profile, download something, start a conversation — versus just share information?
Create or update one lead magnet that solves a real, specific problem your ICP has. Make it something they'd genuinely want even if they never hired you
Write your next post starting with the outcome your ideal client wants — not the service you offer — then work backwards to your expertise

mid.headline: You have content — now build the system around it
mid.text: You're showing up, your content has value, and people are paying attention. The gap is connecting that attention to actual pipeline. Every piece of content you publish should have a clear next step for the right reader — and right now that last mile isn't fully in place.
steps: Add one clear call to action to every piece of content you publish — lead magnet download, DM trigger, or profile visit prompt — so interested readers always have somewhere to go
Promote your lead magnet in your content at least once a week so the people who are already watching you have a reason to raise their hand
Set up a simple email newsletter to capture warm leads so you own a direct line to your audience beyond whatever the algorithm decides to show

high.headline: Your content is doing its job — make sure the system around it keeps up
high.text: You're creating content with real intent and it's paying off. You're earning attention and you have a way to capture it. Now the question is whether every part of your system is pulling the right people into the right next step consistently — not just when things go well.
steps: Track leads generated per post so you know what's actually working — not just what gets the most engagement
Review your lead magnet conversion rate. If people aren't opting in, either the offer or the way you're promoting it needs a fresh look
Find the one point in your content-to-lead journey where people drop off and fix that before adding anything new to the system

answers.label: I search by job title and message anyone who looks like they could be a fit
I target people in the right industry and company size

I look for signals — content engagement, profile activity, shared connections — that suggest they're actually open to a conversation right now
I prioritize warm prospects first: people who've engaged with my content, downloaded a lead magnet, or show a clear trigger that makes the conversation timely

low.headline: Your outreach is asking before it's earned anything
low.text: Your prospects don't owe you a response. They don't know you, they're busy, and your message is competing with a hundred others in their inbox. Before you can ask for anything — a call, a response, even acknowledgment — you need to earn the right to be in that conversation. Right now, your outreach is skipping straight to the ask.
steps: Delete every outreach template that opens with what you do or what you're offering and start from scratch
Write 3 new first messages that lead with something genuinely useful to the specific person you're contacting — no pitch, no ask, no mention of your services in the opener
Rebuild your follow-up sequence so every touchpoint adds something new — not just a reminder that you're waiting on them

mid.headline: Your outreach is moving in the right direction — now make every message feel personal
mid.text: You're thinking about the person on the other end, which already puts you ahead of most people filling inboxes with self-serving pitches. The next level is making every single touchpoint feel like it was written specifically for that one person — not a category of people who share a job title.
steps: Spend 5 focused minutes researching each prospect before you reach out — find one specific thing you can genuinely reference that shows you actually looked
Make sure your first message gives them a reason to respond that has nothing to do with you — an insight, a sharp question, a relevant resource
Review your last 20 outreach conversations and find what the ones that turned into calls had in common — then build your next sequences around that

high.headline: Your outreach builds real relationships instead of burning through contacts — keep going
high.text: You understand that persistence means following up with purpose, and that moving on without entitlement is what separates people who build real pipelines from people who just send more messages. Your results show it. The goal now is to make warm outreach the default, not the exception.
steps: Start warming your best-fit prospects with intentional content engagement before you ever send a message — people respond to people they recognize
Add voice notes or short video messages to your highest-priority outreach conversations — trust builds faster when they can actually hear you
Trace back the clients who came directly from LinkedIn outreach and map out exactly how those relationships started. That's your repeatable blueprint

questions.text: How many hours per week do you spend on LinkedIn — writing content, engaging intentionally, and doing outreach combined?
questions.hint: Count honestly. Scrolling and passively reading don't count. Writing posts, leaving meaningful comments, and sending messages do. We'll multiply by 4 to calculate your monthly investment.

questions.text: On average, how many leads does your LinkedIn activity generate per month?
questions.hint: A lead = someone who raised their hand, booked a call, or directly asked about working with you as a result of LinkedIn — not a cold contact you found there.

questions.text: What is your average deal or monthly retainer size?
questions.hint: Enter the dollar amount of a typical closed deal or monthly retainer. This lets us show you the annual pipeline your current LinkedIn activity is generating — or leaving on the table.

low.headline: You're putting time into LinkedIn without a system to capture what it generates
low.text: LinkedIn is not a posting hobby — it's a business asset. But without a connected system where content earns attention, something captures it, and outreach converts it, you're leaving a lot on the table every single week. The good news is building that system doesn't have to be complicated. It just has to be intentional.
steps: Map out what actually happens after someone engages with your content. Is there a next step for them, or does the opportunity just disappear into the scroll?
Create or promote one lead magnet that gives warm readers a specific reason to raise their hand — not a generic resource, something they'd genuinely want
Set up a simple email newsletter so you own a direct line to your audience that no algorithm can take away from you

mid.headline: Your system exists — now make the pieces talk to each other
mid.text: You have some of the pieces in place but they're probably living in separate lanes. Content happens. Outreach happens. Sometimes a lead shows up. But a real pipeline machine has all three working together and feeding each other — and that connection is what turns LinkedIn from something you do into something that compounds.
steps: Write out step by step what the journey looks like from someone's first impression of your content to a booked call — then find the gaps where people are falling off
Make sure your content actively promotes your lead magnet, and that your lead magnet connects to a nurture sequence that keeps warm leads moving toward a conversation
Start tracking where your leads actually come from so you can put more time into what's working and cut what isn't

high.headline: You have a real system — now protect it and let it compound
high.text: Most people on LinkedIn are guessing. You're not. You have a connected approach and you can see how the pieces work together. Now it's about consistency, measurement, and letting the compounding effect do what it does when you stop starting over.
steps: Document your full system so it can grow with you — a process that only lives in your head is a bottleneck waiting to happen the moment you want to scale or bring in support
Identify the one part of your pipeline right now — content, lead magnet, nurture, or outreach — that's your biggest constraint, and fix that before adding anything new
Set a monthly review of your LinkedIn numbers: leads generated, conversations started, calls booked. That's how you optimize what's already working instead of just doing more of everything
